Moraga.headline: Moraga faces a cold start before light weekend rain returns
Moraga.text: Moraga turns colder overnight, with sheltered spots potentially dipping into the 30s before clouds increase ahead of the next front. Saturday should start mostly quiet, then light rain is expected to arrive late in the day or evening and continue intermittently into Sunday; the broader Bay Area forecast calls for roughly 0.10–0.50 inch, with higher totals in the coastal ranges. Monday looks like the clearest dry break. A stronger Tuesday–Wednesday system could bring more widespread rain and gusty winds, so keep drainage clear while soils remain saturated.

Lafayette.headline: Lafayette gets a chilly pause before another round of rain
Lafayette.text: Lafayette should have a mostly quiet, cold night, with the main question being how quickly clouds arrive and limit valley cooling toward Saturday morning. The next front looks weaker than the storm that just passed, bringing rain mainly late Saturday into Sunday rather than an all-day washout; regional Bay Area totals are forecast around 0.10–0.50 inch, with the higher amounts favored over coastal terrain. Monday offers a welcome dry window. Another, stronger system is expected Tuesday into Wednesday, when renewed rain and gusty winds could affect already-wet ground.

Danville.headline: Danville turns colder before showers return late Saturday
Danville.text: Danville is headed for a chilly night, and the NWS Cold Weather Advisory covers the interior East Bay early Saturday; sheltered valley temperatures could reach the 30s, although incoming clouds may keep some locations closer to the low 40s. Saturday starts mostly dry before a weaker front brings light rain late in the day and into Sunday. Monday should provide a useful break. A stronger system is forecast Tuesday–Wednesday, with more widespread rain and gusty winds possible, so watch drainage and low-lying roads after this week's soaking.

Greenbrook.headline: Danville's Greenbrook area braces for a cold morning and late showers
Greenbrook.text: Danville's Greenbrook area should turn sharply cooler overnight, with the interior East Bay Cold Weather Advisory in effect early Saturday and sheltered locations at risk of dipping into the 30s. Clouds increase ahead of a weaker front, keeping the first part of Saturday relatively quiet before light rain spreads in late Saturday and may linger into Sunday. Monday is the best opportunity for a dry reset. A stronger Pacific system approaches Tuesday–Wednesday, bringing another round of rain and gustier winds that could aggravate runoff in already-wet neighborhoods.

Marin City.headline: Marin City gets a brief lull before rain and higher bay tides
Marin City.text: Marin City should see a quieter, cool stretch into Saturday, with bay-side temperatures generally less prone to the sharp valley chill expected inland. A weaker front brings rain late Saturday into Sunday, followed by a mainly dry Monday; the more consequential concern arrives Tuesday–Wednesday as another storm overlaps the November king-tide cycle. The NWS says 2–3 feet of coastal inundation is possible at vulnerable Bay shoreline locations during peak tides, with runoff or storm surge potentially worsening impacts. Keep an eye on low-lying access roads and waterfront areas.

Sausalito.headline: Sausalito's waterfront gets a short break before king tides and rain
Sausalito.text: Sausalito should have a mostly quiet, cool start to the weekend, although clouds will increase before a weaker front brings rain late Saturday into Sunday. Monday looks like a brief pause, but the pattern turns more active Tuesday and Wednesday with another round of rain and stronger winds possible near the coast. The larger waterfront concern is the king-tide cycle: the NWS says 2–3 feet of inundation is possible at vulnerable Bay shoreline locations during peak tides, and rain runoff or storm surge could add to the water level. Watch low-lying roads and shoreline access.

Brentwood.headline: Brentwood gets a foggy, chilly pause before a wetter holiday week
Brentwood.text: Brentwood should turn mostly dry tonight, but cold temperatures and patchy Delta-area fog are possible early Saturday, especially around low-lying routes. The weekend front is weaker than the recent storm and should bring only light, spotty rain late Saturday into Sunday, although exact totals around the Delta remain uncertain. Monday looks like a short break. Rain chances increase again Tuesday into Wednesday as a stronger system moves inland, but current guidance suggests this system should be less potent than the last; keep watching for updates as the holiday period approaches.

East Sacramento.headline: East Sacramento gets a cold, fog-prone morning before rain returns
East Sacramento.text: East Sacramento should turn mostly dry tonight, then start Saturday cold with areas of fog and patchy frost possible around the Valley. A weaker system brings light rain late Saturday into Sunday, with the Sacramento office expecting around 0.10 inch or less across most Valley locations; showers may persist longer farther north and over the foothills. Monday is forecast to be briefly dry. A stronger system returns Tuesday into Wednesday, and NWS guidance puts the Sacramento Valley chance of at least an inch at 50–70%, though this system should be less potent than the last.
